findings.title: Domain Compromise via NTLM Relay + DCSync
findings.description: SMB signing is disabled on the majority of hosts in the CORP.LOCAL domain. An NTLM relay attack was performed using Responder and ntlmrelayx, capturing authentication from FS01 and relaying it to SQL01. Combined with DCSync rights obtained via the svc_backup service account, full domain compromise was achieved within 4 hours of initial access.
findings.recommendation: Enable and enforce SMB signing across all domain-joined hosts via GPO. Implement tiered administration model. Review service account privileges and rotate all compromised credentials.
findings.notes: CVSS: 10.0 Critical. Demonstrated full domain compromise.

findings.title: EternalBlue (MS17-010) on End-of-Life Windows Server 2008 R2
findings.description: LEGACY-SRV01 is running Windows Server 2008 R2, which is past end-of-life and no longer receives security patches. The host is confirmed vulnerable to MS17-010 (EternalBlue), the critical SMBv1 vulnerability exploited by WannaCry and NotPetya ransomware. This host is accessible from the server VLAN.
findings.recommendation: Immediately decommission or isolate LEGACY-SRV01. If decommission is not immediately possible, block inbound SMB (TCP 445) at the firewall/VLAN boundary and disable SMBv1.

findings.title: Credentials Stored in Plaintext on File Server
findings.description: Plaintext credentials for VMware ESXi (esxadmin) and the svc_backup service account were found stored in a text file at D:\VMware\creds.txt on FS01. These credentials provided access to the hypervisor infrastructure and were used to escalate from a low-privileged SMB relay session to full domain and hypervisor administrator.
findings.recommendation: Remove all plaintext credential stores. Implement a PAM/secrets manager solution (e.g. CyberArk, HashiCorp Vault). Review file server share permissions to enforce least privilege.
findings.notes: Root cause of hypervisor and significant lateral movement.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Jenkins and Jupyter Notebook on Developer Server
findings.description: The Jenkins CI/CD server on LNXDEV01 port 8080 and Jupyter Notebook on port 8888 are accessible without authentication from the server network. Jenkins has script console access (Groovy), enabling arbitrary OS command execution. Jupyter notebooks can execute arbitrary Python. Historical Git repositories on this host contain hardcoded AWS access keys.
findings.recommendation: Immediately require authentication for all developer tools. Audit and rotate any exposed API keys/secrets found in version control history. Restrict network access to developer tools to the workstation VLAN only.

findings.title: OpenVPN Access Server with Default Credentials and No MFA
findings.description: The internet-facing OpenVPN Access Server admin panel (port 943) is accessible with default credentials (admin/password). Multi-factor authentication is not enforced for VPN users, meaning captured domain credentials can be used directly to establish VPN access without additional verification.
findings.recommendation: Change default admin credentials immediately. Enforce MFA for all VPN connections. Restrict admin panel access to management network only.
findings.notes: Combination of default creds and no MFA creates easy external entry point.

findings.title: Weak and Reused Service Account Passwords
findings.description: Multiple service accounts (svc_backup, svc_sql, sa) were found with weak or default passwords that were trivially cracked offline. The svc_backup account has local administrator rights on domain controllers and critical servers, significantly amplifying the blast radius of its compromise.
findings.recommendation: Implement a password policy requiring minimum 20-character passwords for service accounts. Use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA) where possible. Apply principle of least privilege to all service accounts.
